G9325.definition:
1.  put together, composite, compound  , (Plato Philosophus):  complex  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2.  put together, fictitious  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3.  metaphorically   agreed upon  , ἐκ συνθέτου  by agreement  , Lat.  ex composito , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9326.definition:
1.  a composition  , of words and sentences, (Lucian) 
2.  a conventional agreement, convention, compact  , (Plato Philosophus); ἐκ συνθήκης,  ex composito, by agreement  , (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ συνθήκην  conventionally  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3.  the article of a compact   or  treaty  , (Thucydides):—;mostly in  plural   the articles of agreement  , and collectively,  a contract, compact, covenant, treaty  , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; συνθήκας ποιέεσθαί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν συνθηκῶν according to  the covenant  , (Isocrates Orator); κατὰ τὰς ς. (Thucydides) (ML)

G9327.definition:
1.  knowing along with   another,  conscious  , ὡς θεοὶ ξυνίστορες as the gods are  witnesses  , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
2. with  accusative  (with the verbal construction), πολλὰ συνίστορα κακά  conscious of   many evils, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9332.definition:
1.  to make to live with  , (Isocrates Orator); ς. τινὶ τὴν θυγατέρα  to give   him one's daughter  in marriage  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  to combine in one city, unite under a capital   or  metropolis  , ξ. πάντας (i.e. ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας)) (Thucydides):—;Pass., ξυνοικισθείσης πόλεως the city having  been regularly formed  , opposite to κατὰ κώμας οἰκίζεσθαι, (Thucydides) 
3.  to join in peopling   or  colonising   a country, (Euripides) 
4. generally  to unite, associate  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9335.definition:
1.  that which is put together in order  :

3.  the constitution of a state  , ς. πολιτείας  a form   of constitution, (Isocrates Orator) 
4.  an arrangement of musical notes  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5.  a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine  , (Plutarch)

G9336.definition:
1.  a putting together, arranging, arrangement, organisation, order  , (Thucydides):  rule  , (Demosthenes Orator)

G9344.definition: to weave together  :  metaphorically   to frame with art, devise cunningly  , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ὥστε ταῦτα συνυφανθῆναι so that this  web was woven  , i. e. this business undertaken, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9348.definition:
1.  a pipe  :

 (ML)

G9349.definition:

G9359.definition:

G9366.definition:
1. Lat. fall-o (the sigma being lost):—;  to make to fall, throw down, overthrow  , properly  by tripping up, to trip up in wrestling  , (Homer), etc.; σφ. ναῦς  to throw   her  on her beam-ends  , (Plutarch); ἵππος σφ. τὸν ἀναβάτην  throws   him, (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass.  to be tripped up  , (Aristophanes Comicus); of a drunken man, σφαλλόμενος  reeling, staggering  , (Aristophanes Comicus)

3.  to baffle, foil, balk, disappoint  , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass.  to err, go wrong, be mistaken  , (Herdotus Historicus)

 (ML)

suffering, wretched  , Lat.  miser , (Odyssey by Homer); ὦ τάλαιν᾽ ἐγώ (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὦ τάλαν (Sophocles Tragicus);—;with  genitive  causae, τάλαιν᾽ ἐγὼ τῆς ὕβρεως  wretched that I am   for this insolence, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in bad sense, τάλαν  wretch!   (Odyssey by Homer)—; comparative  τᾶλάντερος, η, ον: Sup. τᾶλάντατος, η, ον, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 τᾶλα_; doric also τᾶλᾶς:  vocative  τάλᾶν. (ML)

G9398.definition:
1.  one who carves and distributes, a dispenser  , (Iliad by Homer):—;of Zeus, as  the dispenser   of all things to men, (Iliad by Homer); so Aeolus is τ. ἀνέμων (Odyssey by Homer):—;of kings or rulers,  a controller, director  , (Pindar); τ. κώμων  master   of the revels, (Pindar); τ. Διός  the priest   of Zeus, (Pindar): τ. Μοισᾶν, i. e. a poet, (Pindar); οἶκος τ. στεφάνων  that hath store   of crowns, (Pindar); τῆς τε ἐπιθυμίας καὶ τῆς τύχης τ.  controller   both of his desire and of fortune, (Thucydides); τ. τριαίνης, of Poseidon, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. in Prose,  a controller   of payments,  treasurer  , (Herdotus Historicus); τ. τοῦ ἱροῦ  the controller   of the sacred treasure in the citadel of Athens, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. at Rome,  the quaestor  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9399.definition:
1.  to be controller   of receipts and expenditure,  to be treasurer, paymaster  , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with  genitive , τ. τῆς Παράλου  to be paymaster of   the Paralus, (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. at Rome,  to be quaestor  , (Plutarch) 
3.  transitive   to deal out, dispense  , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Pass., τοὺς νόμους τεταμιεύμεθα  we have   the laws  dealt out  , (Lysias Orator):—;Mid., ταμιεύεσθαι εἰς ὅσον βουλόμεθα ἄρχειν  to control   the limits to which we mean to extend our sway, (Thucydides) 
4. of keeping house,  to regulate, manage  , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; Pass., χώρα ταμιευομένα τινί  governed   or  possessed   by one, (Pindar) 
5.  to store up  , (Demosthenes Orator); Ζηνὸς ταμιεύεσκε γονάς  she was the depository of   it, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)
